simple.meaning: אוּלָם (ʼûwlâm) is a Hebrew word meaning “however or on the contrary.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אוּלָם (H199) appears 19 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Genesis 28:19, with occurrences in Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, Judges, 1 Samuel, and 3 more.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אוּלָם (H199) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אוּלָם (H199) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אוּלָם (ʼûwlâm) / H199 is traced through Genesis 28:19, Genesis 48:19, Exodus 9:16, Numbers 14:21 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.usage: as for, but, howbeit, in very deed, surely, truly, wherefore.
definitions.full: H199. ulam III. אוּלָם and ( Job 17:10 , perhaps for sake of assonance with following כֻּלָּם ) אֻלָּם adverb but, but indeed, a strong adversative Job 2:5 ; 5:8 ; 13:3 (where ᵐ5 excellently οὐ μὴν ἀλλά ). More usually with וְאוּלָם וְ, Gen 28:19 (compare Judg 18:29 ) Gen 48:19 howbeit his younger brother shall be greater than he, Exod 9:16 but in very deed , Num 14:21 (compare 1Sam 20:3 ; 25:34 ) 1Kin 20:23 ; Micah 3:8 ; Job 1:11 ; 11:5 ; 12:7 ; 13:4 ; 14:18 ; 17:10 ; 33:1 . I. און (compare Arabic (medial ) be fatigued, tired , weariness, sorrow, trouble ). **On etymology, compare also Bev Jphil. xxvi. 300-2 .
